Documentation\n\nThis document provides an overview of the FastAPI Realworld Example App, covering its purpose, key components, data flow, and dependencies.\n\n## Purpose\n\nThe FastAPI Realworld Example App aims to provide a comprehensive and well-structured backend implementation using FastAPI, adhering to the Realworld API specification. It serves as a reference for building robust and scalable web applications with Python and FastAPI.\n\n## Key Components\n\n-   **`app/`**: Contains the main application code.\n    -   **`api/`**: Handles web-related aspects, including dependencies, error handling, and route definitions.\n    -   **`core/`**: Manages application configuration, startup events, and logging.\n    -   **`db/`**: Deals with database interactions, including Alembic migrations and CRUD operations.\n    -   **`models/`**: Defines Pydantic models for the application, including domain models and schemas for web routes.\n    -   **`resources/`**: Stores string resources used in web responses.\n    -   **`services/`**: Implements business logic beyond basic CRUD operations.\n    -   **`main.py`**: Initializes and configures the FastAPI application.\n-   **`tests/`**: Contains all the tests for the project, utilizing `pytest`.\n-   **`postman/`**: Includes Postman collection for API testing.\n-   **`scripts/`**: Provides utility scripts for formatting, linting, and testing.\n\n## Data Flow\n\nData typically enters the application through API routes defined in `app/api/routes/`. These routes interact with services (in `app/services/`) or repositories (in `app/db/repositories/`) to perform business logic and database operations. Pydantic models in `app/models/` are used for request and response validation. Data is persisted in the PostgreSQL database, managed via Alembic migrations (`app/db/migrations/`).\n\n## Dependencies\n\n-   **Internal**: The application is modular, with components in `app/` depending on each other. Key internal dependencies include FastAPI, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy (via Alembic), and `pytest` for testing.\n-   **External**: PostgreSQL is the primary external dependency for data storage. Environment variables (e.g., `DATABASE_URL`, `SECRET_KEY`) are crucial for configuration.\n\n## Configuration\n\nConfiguration is primarily managed through environment variables, with an example `.env.example` file provided. The `app/core/settings` module likely handles the loading and validation of these settings.\n\n## Running the Application\n\nInstructions for setting up PostgreSQL, installing dependencies with Poetry, and running the application with `uvicorn` and Alembic are provided in the README.\n\n## Testing\n\nTests are located in the `tests/` directory and can be run using the `pytest` command. The `DATABASE_URL` environment variable needs to be configured for tests to run.\n\n## Deployment with Docker\n\nDocker and Docker Compose can be used for deployment, with instructions provided for setting up the database and application containers.\n\n## Project Structure Visualisation\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n    A[app] --> A1[api]\n    A1 --> A1_1[dependencies]\n    A1 --> A1_2[errors]\n    A1 --> A1_3[routes]\n    A --> A2[core]\n    A --> A3[db]\n    A3 --> A3_1[migrations]\n    A3 --> A3_2[repositories]\n    A --> A4[models]\n    A4 --> A4_1[domain]\n    A4 --> A4_2[schemas]\n    A --> A5[resources]\n    A --> A6[services]\n    A --> A7[main.py]\n    B[tests] --> B1[test_api]\n    B1 --> B1_1[test_errors]\n    B1 --> B1_2[test_routes]\n    B --> B2[test_db]\n    B --> B3[test_schemas]\n    B --> B4[test_services]\n    C[postman]\n    D[scripts]\n```\n\n## Code Snippets\n\n**Environment Variable Setup (from `README.rst`)**\n\n```bash\ntouch .env\necho APP_ENV=dev >> .env\necho DATABASE_URL=postgresql://$POSTGRES_USER:$POSTGRES_PASSWORD@$POSTGRES_HOST:$POSTGRES_PORT/$POSTGRES_DB >> .env\necho SECRET_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 32) >> .env\n```\n\n**Running the Application (from `README.rst`)**\n\n```bash\nalembic upgrade head\nuvicorn app.main:app --reload\n```\n\n**Running Tests (from `README.rst`)**\n\n```bash\npytest\n```\n\n## Note on Maintenance\n\nThe `README.rst` indicates that this repository is not actively maintained as it fulfills its primary goal of passing the Conduit test suite. Example App aims to provide a comprehensive and well-structured backend implementation using FastAPI, adhering to the Realworld API specification. It serves as a reference for building robust and scalable web applications with Python and FastAPI.\n\n## Key Components\n\n-   **`app/`**: Contains the main application code.\n    -   **`api/`**: Handles web-related aspects, including dependencies, error handling, and route definitions.\n    -   **`core/`**: Manages application configuration, startup events, and logging.\n    -   **`db/`**: Deals with database interactions, including Alembic migrations and CRUD operations.\n    -   **`models/`**: Defines Pydantic models for the application, including domain models and schemas for web routes.\n    -   **`resources/`**: Stores string resources used in web responses.\n    -   **`services/`**: Implements business logic beyond basic CRUD operations.\n    -   **`main.py`**: Initializes and configures the FastAPI application.\n-   **`tests/`**: Contains all the tests for the project, utilizing `pytest`.\n-   **`postman/`**: Includes Postman collection for API testing.\n-   **`scripts/`**: Provides utility scripts for formatting, linting, and testing.\n\n## Data Flow\n\nData typically enters the application through API routes defined in `app/api/routes/`. These routes interact with services (in `app/services/`) or repositories (in `app/db/repositories/`) to perform business logic and database operations.
